compensatable — before the point of no return; a failure downstream reverses it.
pivot — the point of no return.
retriable — after the pivot; no compensation exists, so the only path is to retry until it succeeds.
Splitting the slice out to `:3103` is named and deferred.
The reopen condition, stated so it is not a matter of taste.

title: The record search aggregator fans out per request and ranks nothing
readWhen: searching records across services — no client-side index, ever, and a source's search member is validated at module load
summary: `GET /api/search` on the Next host fans out to the sources it mounts, carrying the caller's own session, and returns grouped results. No index, ever.

title: The sidebar renders the taxonomy, and a shell may ask about the viewport
readWhen: rendering navigation — type › domain › destination, and auto-collapse must never write the stored preference
summary: Three tiers — type › domain › destination — and `NavItem` has no children, so a fourth is unsayable. #113 asked for the cap to live "in the type, not by convention"; an interface in which deeper nesting cannot be expressed is the strongest available form of that.

title: The workspace address is the taxonomy serialized
readWhen: addressing a workspace tab — `master:<key>[:<id>]` is one grammar, and both version constants bump when it changes
summary: `master:product-brand` is the list, `master:product-brand:abc123` is one record. `system:configuration` becomes `master:configuration`.

title: The optimistic mutation contract, and reconciliation is a re-query
readWhen: a write answers `202` — the browser keeps watching, and a `404` from the tracker means not-tracked-yet, never failed
summary:
Announce after the shape assertion, never before.
Reopen condition: a pending set that routinely reaches its cap.
`TabState`'s two unwritten values stay unwritten, on purpose.

title: The command palette owns no index, and its depth is a page stack
readWhen: adding anything to the command palette — the sources filter and the control renders, and matching is accent-folded because the default locale is Spanish
summary:
Record groups are deliberately exempt.
The auth-service route moves from `requirePrincipal` to `requirePermission(SIGN_OUT_OTHERS)`, so the grant is real authorization rather than a filter on an…
Every role holds it.

title: The wizard: a step graph, a draft above the forms, and a submit that hands off
readWhen: building a multi-step screen — the step graph is data, Back pops a history stack, and a validation gate belongs to a step
summary:
Load time, not step time.
Neither `TABS_VERSION` nor `DRAFTS_VERSION` bumps.

title: A convention that is only stated is a convention that gets skipped
readWhen: adding a working convention, or wondering why attribution trailers keep reappearing — a convention that is only stated is one that gets skipped
summary:
A working convention gets a check, and the check owns one predicate that every surface calls.
The canonical casing is git's, not the documentation's.
An exemption only means something for a path the scan can reach.

title: Authoring an offering, and publication as a verb rather than a field
readWhen: authoring or publishing an offering — `published → published` is legal, and `status` is server-owned or the verb is decoration
summary:
The field is hidden.
`status` had to stop being `required`.
Recorded residual: there is no publish-from-the-list affordance.
`published → published` is legal.
`unpublish` from anything but `published` fails.

title: Announcing a publication, and a shared contract to announce it with
readWhen: emitting or consuming a publication — the projector orders on `publishedAt`, and an unpublication leaves a tombstone because a delete has nothing to be ordered by
summary: `product-configuration-management` authors the publication and `marketplace-catalog` projects it. A `business:domain` package may never depend on another, so the payload cannot be shared through either of them; that is the constraint ADR 0047 named when it deferred this.

title: The publication snapshot carries what the storefront renders
readWhen: adding a member to the publication snapshot — optional is a safety property, and an absent member is written absent, never `undefined`
summary:
It is ordered before the price check.
And it refuses a publication only, never a takedown.

title: Rebuilding the published catalog from tenant storage
readWhen: the storefront is empty after a reset, or a publication was lost — the rebuild walk re-emits from tenant storage and must never stamp `now`
summary:
the event id is `<offeringId>:<publishedAt>`, so a re-stamped moment makes the message a new publication rather than a redelivery — the outbox's unique index…
and it overwrites the projection's ordering key, so a genuine `catalog.unpublished` emitted a second earlier is then read as stale and ignored.
It is server-owned, so it is neither `readonly` nor `required`.
Chained to the seed, not merged beside it.

title: The storefront reads the projection
readWhen: the storefront reads or renders catalog data — nothing is enumerated at build time, and a failed read renders an empty catalog and logs
summary:
The lookup is `load` with a filter, never `get`.
The cost is stated rather than hidden: empty and broken render identically.
This is correctness, not a lost optimization.
Empty and absent are different, and the difference is which routes it reaches.
Order is the mechanism.

title: The checkout saga: a definition that is data, and a compensation that is told what it undid
readWhen: a flow spans two services and one of them may have to be undone — the definition is data, a fan-out step compensates only the calls that succeeded, and a participant the saga may retry must be idempotent on the command id
summary:
A fan-out step compensates exactly the calls that succeeded.
The tempting wrong answer is to call the order write the pivot.
Without this, an at-least-once dispatch oversells.
It walks one database, not many.
It writes back. A publish is done when the broker acks it; a command's response is the step's outcome, and it must be recorded before the next step is…

title: Scoping a platform-plane read to its caller, and a receipt that needs no session
readWhen: a read has to be narrowed to whoever is asking, or an anonymous buyer has to be shown something that is theirs — the scope is conjoined onto the load request and never expressed as a query, and a receipt is carried rather than read back
summary:
Absent means no party, never any party.
Not by concatenating rsql.
`partyRole` selects a predicate; it grants nothing.
The operator's wider read is not a permission of its own, and that is a constraint rather than a preference.
A caller who owns nothing gets an empty page rather than a refusal.

title: Capture is the pivot, and the bus carries what follows
readWhen: money has to be taken inside a flow, or a saga step fails after the point of no return — capture is a dispatched step and never a subscription, and a post-pivot failure rolls forward or strands, never back
summary:
Before the pivot — unchanged.
After the pivot — never compensate.
`fanOutFrom` — the conversion had nothing to address.
Body templates — the capture had nothing to attach to.
The template lives in the caller's `inputs`, never in the definition.

title: A coordinator resumes from its own record, and a dispatch needs no outbox
readWhen: a saga has to survive its coordinator dying, or you are about to build the command outbox two earlier records specify — the instance is already the durable record of intent, and where to resume is derived from the outcomes rather than stored beside them
summary:
Two records of one fact can disagree, and this pair would have to be written in the same breath.
The second row is the one that would oversell.
A second replica's claim finds the instance no longer stale and skips it.
This sweep's next tick does not re-pick the instance it is still working on.
The staleness window must stay above the longest a step legitimately takes.

title: The counter sale is the checkout saga, and the till holds no secret
readWhen: a vendor sells somewhere other than the storefront, or a browser surface needs to start a flow that writes another slice's store — the sale is the same saga with a channel on it, and the decision is made where a session can actually be verified
summary: No new flow, no new definition, no second path into stock or settlement. The till's sale runs the same four steps — reserve, write the order, capture, convert the hold — and differs only in what rides on two of the inputs: a `RelatedChannel` copy on the order, a `channelId` and…

title: Settlement joins the sale to its payment, and the ledger states its own base
readWhen: pricing a vendor's commission, or a consumer needs data that no single event on the bus carries — the fold joins two messages on the order id, and a payout is the gross less the cut rather than the sum of the cuts
summary:
Arrival order is not assumed in either direction.
The fold's claim is conditional, not merely guarded.
Rejected: an HTTP read into order-service.
Rejected: widening `payment.captured`. payment-service does not hold the lines either.
`saleAmount` — the vendor's subtotal for that order, before the cut.

title: The order after payment: fulfil, cancel, refund, and a capability the coordinator never sees
readWhen: a paid order has to move again, or an anonymous buyer has to be authorized for a write — the cancel is a saga whose pivot is a refund, and the buyer's capability is a digest at rest because the order write is itself a saga step
summary:
The converse is also true, and the build found it the expensive way: the status cannot do `sagaCommandId`'s job either.
A sequential run proves nothing here.
The `201` is a saga step outcome.
The entity envelope has no slot for a sibling field.
A key is a thing to rotate.

title: entifix leaves the repo, and r10c becomes one of its consumers
readWhen: looking for the framework's source, changing entifix while r10c runs, or wondering why a framework file imports a cookie name from core instead of declaring its own — the boundary is wide but composable, and every r10c-specific value crosses a seam rather than being imported
summary:
entifix is extracted into `r10c-technologies/entifix` and published as `@entifix/*`, with r10c as one of two external consumers.
The invariant that enforces this is not about direction.
A value, not a path.
The typed-key gate is the one seam that cannot be split.
The rename rewrites identifiers in 29 existing records and revises none of them.
